records.transcript:
Freedom of Information Team
Wales Office
Gwydyr House
Whitehall
London █████

cc: █████ — the mailbox that sent the acknowledgement and the response

Dear Sir or Madam,

Request for Internal Review — 26FOI 103 — response dated 22 September 2026
Requester: Requester

I request an internal review of the handling and substance of 26FOI 103.

This is an FOI review only. I am not asking the Wales Office to determine title, to reopen BP Properties Ltd v Buckler, or to adopt any party's case on the land. I am asking whether the letter of 22 September 2026 answered the request that was made, and whether the search described in it was adequate.

A. What is already on this file

1. 29 August 2026 — I asked the Wales Office for recorded information about Great House Farm. Your letter of 22 September quotes the request as five points. I adopt that quotation. The points were:

- records of any communication or outreach between Cadw, or its predecessor functions, and the Office of the Secretary of State for Wales / Welsh Office concerning Great House Farm during July–December 1988;
- records of any recommendation, briefing, submission, notification or formal appeal concerning the protection or listing of Great House Farm submitted to the Secretary of State;
- records of any communications with the occupiers and owners of the property before the refusal decision of 5 December 1988;
- any surviving destruction, disposal, transfer or accession documentation relating to the Great House Farm 1988 assessment file, including certificates, dockets, lists, database entries, retention schedules, disposal authorities or other contemporaneous records held by the Welsh Office, its predecessors, Cadw, or any repository to which relevant records were transferred;
- information regarding a decision made in relation to Great House Farm in 1988, including the evidence that was used to support that decision.

2. 8 September 2026 — acknowledgement from NIO FOI (█████), recording the request date as 29/08/26. It named no officer and described no search.

3. 22 September 2026 — covering email from the same NIO FOI mailbox, attaching “26FOI 103 - Buckler - Response.pdf”. The covering email contained no substance. The letter is signed Freedom of Information Team, Wales Office, and directs any review to █████.

This review is within the two calendar months stated in that letter. The deadline you gave is 22 November 2026.

B. What the letter actually █████, and what it does not

The operative paragraph is this:

“We have carried out a search of our digital records and have determined that the Wales Office does not hold the information requested. Any paper files previously held by the former Welsh Office relating to this matter would have been transferred to the National Assembly for Wales in 1999, and subsequently to the Welsh Government in 2007.”

That paragraph does not answer the request. The gaps are these.

1. Digital records only. The letter █████ a search of digital records. It does not say that paper, microfilm, card indexes, transfer lists, accession registers, or destruction schedules were searched. A 1988 Welsh Office file is a paper file. A search confined to current digital holdings cannot find it, and cannot find the transfer or destruction docket that the fourth bullet asked for.

2. “Would have been transferred” is not a search result. It is an assumption about devolution. It is not a statement that a transfer list was consulted, that a file for this house appears on that list, or that the file was received in Cardiff. “Would have been” covers three different outcomes: transferred, destroyed, or still here under another description. The letter does not distinguish them.

3. The fourth bullet asked for the transfer, disposal and accession records themselves. Those records, if they exist, are Wales Office records of what left the building. They are not the assessment file. Pointing me to the Welsh Government does not answer a request for the docket, the list, the database entry or the disposal authority. Those may still be held here even if the file went to Cardiff. The letter does not say they were searched for.

4. The five bullets are not answered one by one. There is no finding on communications with Cadw; no finding on any briefing or appeal to the Secretary of State; no finding on communications with occupiers and owners before 5 December 1988; no finding on the evidence said to have supported a 1988 decision. A single sentence that digital records do not hold “the information requested” does not show that each limb was searched.

5. The letter uses “the refusal decision of 5 December 1988” only because I used it. It does not say whether that decision is recognised, whether a file for it was identified, or whether the decision is one of the papers “which would have been transferred”. Silence on a dated decision is not a not-held finding.

6. “You may therefore wish” is not section 16 advice. Section 16 requires advice and assistance so far as reasonable. A reasonable step, where the department asserts a transfer, is to give the receiving body's file reference, the date of transfer, and the series. None is given. If the intention was section 21 (information reasonably accessible elsewhere), that exemption is not named, and the conditions are not addressed. A suggestion that I write to █████ is not a section 21 notice.

7. “Does not hold” is stated as a conclusion. The search described cannot support it. A not-held finding under section 1 requires a search capable of finding the information. A search of digital records, plus an assumption about 1999, is not that search.

8. The request was answered from a Northern Ireland Office mailbox. The letter is in the name of the Wales Office. The review must be of the Wales Office search. Please confirm it will not be taken by the person who signed the 22 September letter.

C. What the reviewing officer is asked to determine

1. What was searched, by name: digital systems, paper series, transfer lists, accession registers, destruction schedules, Gwydyr House holdings, and any index of files passed to the National Assembly in 1999 or to the Welsh Government in 2007. If a location was not searched, say so.

2. For each of the five bullets, a separate finding: held, not held after the searches at (1), transferred (with date, recipient and reference), or destroyed (with date and disposal authority).

3. Whether any transfer, disposal or accession record relating to a Great House Farm 1988 assessment file is held by this department, as distinct from the assessment file itself.

4. Whether any record of a decision on or about 5 December 1988, or of communications with the occupiers or owners before that date, was identified even as an index entry.

5. If information is held and is not to be disclosed, a section 17 notice naming the exemption. Do not replace that notice with a referral.

6. If the review maintains that the file went to Cardiff, the transfer reference. Without it, the referral is an assertion.

D. Scope, so the review is not narrowed again

The window is July–December 1988. Possession of Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough, adjoining St Dochdwy's, was taken on 29 November 1988. Demolition of the farmhouse began on 6 December 1988. The refusal date in the request is 5 December 1988. Those dates fix the search. They do not ask you to decide the land.

I have made a parallel request to the Welsh Government, following the referral. That does not discharge 26FOI 103. A file can have been transferred and the transfer docket can still be here. Both questions were asked. Only one was gestured at.

E. Why these records are in scope, without asking you to decide title

The public index is https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/

The investigation distinguishes Parcel A (farmhouse, garden, buildings and yard — the family's maintained freehold interest out of the Bute estate) from Parcel B (eastern fields). Later papers use “whole farm”. BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 decided possession, limitation and the October 1974 letters. It did not decide the documentary root of Parcel A. Whether the Secretary of State or Cadw looked at this house in the week it was refused and pulled down is a records question. It is not a request that you adopt the family's case.

F. Preservation

Please preserve any record that may fall within 26FOI 103 while this review is open, including transfer lists, destruction schedules and anything due for routine disposal. Do not transfer or destroy in-scope material without a written receipt that can be disclosed on the review.

G. Reservation

This letter does not waive any position on title, registration, concealment, limitation, or any later reopening. It is an internal review under the Freedom of Information Act 2000. It is not a claim form and is not service of proceedings.

Please acknowledge receipt, give the review reference, and state the date by which the review will be completed. ICO guidance is that an internal review should normally be completed within 20 working days.

Yours faithfully,

Requester 
█████

Information Governance Team
Vale of Glamorgan Council
█████
cc: █████

Sirs/Madam,

New request under FOIA 2000 and/or EIR 2004. Do not treat this as a reopening or expansion of 00210772, 00211463 or 00211484. Those cases stay as they are.

Land: Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Leckwith Road, Llandough, later Church View Close.
Applications: 89/01396/OUT (outline granted 13 March 1990) and 92/00671/RES.

I already have, or have already asked for, the officer's report, Policy H.2 text, Appendices C–E, the decision notices, and the general archaeological-condition papers. This request is confined to classes that those earlier requests did not name.

Please disclose recorded information held, or confirm item by item if not held:

1. Section 52 / later section 106 / land charges
Any agreement under section 52 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1971, any later section 106 instrument, any deed, undertaking or other agreement regulating the development or use of this land, and any corresponding entry on the local land charges register. Search legal, planning and land-charges holdings, not only the 2026 planning-file scan. If none is held, say so expressly. That is an open records question, not a conclusion that none existed.

2. Historic planning register
The planning-register entries that the Town and Country Planning General Development Order 1988 required the authority to keep for 89/01396/OUT and 92/00671/RES: the applications, reserved-matters applications, plans and drawings, and relevant decision information. If the 2026 file disclosure is incomplete against that register, say what the register still lists and what is missing from the file.

3. Appendix B
Appendix B to the officer's report on 89/01396/OUT: the further GGAT comments after discussions with the Trust. Case 00211463 asked for C, D and E and for a list of annexes. It did not ask for B by that description. If B is not held, say when it left the file, under what retention rule, and whether any copy survives elsewhere.

4. Condition 16–18 chain
Named papers, not a general search:
(a) conditions 16, 17 and 18 as issued on the 13 March 1990 permission;
(b) the Council's October 1990 confirmation of condition 17;
(c) GGAT's archaeological warning of July 1992;
(d) the September 1992 reserved-matters approval, and whether any further archaeological condition was attached;
(e) the 1993–94 papers on whether condition 18 had been discharged, including GGAT's December 1993 letters recommending a breach-of-condition notice.

5. Environmental assessment / screening
Any preliminary environmental-assessment determination, screening opinion, or recorded decision that an environmental statement was or was not required for 89/01396/OUT. The application site is described as about 3.4 acres / 1.38 hectares. I am not asserting that an environmental statement was required. I am asking whether the Council made and recorded the determination at all.

6. Archaeological-interest consultation route
Any record of the statutory consultation route actually used because the land was recorded in the county Sites and Monuments Record, or was treated as a "site of archaeological interest" under the 1988 Order. I am not asking you to treat SMR status as automatic proof of a particular duty. I am asking what route was used.

7. Application receipt date
The Council's receipt record for 89/01396/OUT. The application form is dated October 1989. The reconstructed planning record gives 8 November 1989 as receipt of the application and plans. Please supply the date-stamped receipt, validation or register entry.

8. 92/00671/RES completeness and applicant standing
(a) A file list or register for 92/00671/RES showing what the reserved-matters file originally contained.
(b) Any sale, option, conditional-contract or authority-to-apply paper on the planning files covering the change from BP Properties (1989 outline applicant) to Ideal Homes Wales (appearing on the 1992 reserved-matters trail), including the recorded BP-to-Ideal Homes transfer of 3 December 1993.
This is a documentary interest/authority question. It is not an allegation that the 1992 application was invalid.

If a record is not held, say so for that item. If it was destroyed, transferred or archived, give the date, the schedule, and any surviving catalogue. Search planning, legal, land charges and archived/scanned holdings.

Please give a new reference and the 20 working-day date. Preserve anything in scope.

The public evidence index is https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/ . I am not asking the Council to decide title.

Yours faithfully,

Requester

News desks,

I am not asking you to adopt a legal conclusion. I am asking you to look at a primary record that is now public, before more of it is lost.

https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/

What the record shows, as distinct from what is still a question:

Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr stood by St Dochdwy's, Llandough. Possession was taken on 29 November 1988. Demolition of the farmhouse began on 6 December 1988. The land is now Church View Close. The current registered proprietor of WA231076 is Persimmon Homes (Wales) Ltd. First-registration applications were made on 30 November 1982 (WA231076) and 23 February 1983 (WA240304, later closed into WA231076).

A Vale of Glamorgan internal review requested on 7 July (00210772) has no outcome. HM Land Registry file N610CGV is with the Independent Complaints Reviewer. A replica of the house is being built in the Welsh settlement in Patagonia as a museum, not as restitution.

Contemporary reporting described the 1988 scene in the language of a battleground. I can supply documents and a named contact.

Yours faithfully,

Requester

Sirs/ Ma'ams,

I need to correct a date I have used in earlier correspondence about Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough, titles WA231076 and WA240304.

I had treated 1983 as the year the two titles were merged. That was wrong. HM Land Registry’s own letter of 23 March 2026 (Lisa Griffiths, ref N610CGV) separates the two acts.
1982–83 was first registration of two live titles, not a merger.
30 November 1982: application to first-register WA231076. The Court of Appeal later treated BP Properties Ltd as registered proprietors of “the farm” from November 1982.
23 February 1983: application to first-register a second title, WA240304.
26 March 1983: Mary Williams died. On the family’s case, notice of those applications did not reach us until after her death, while the family was in mourning. She had no window in which to object. The family was not in a position to use any window that arrived after that.
Those two titles remained separate through first instance.
24 July 1986: Hollis J. Both titles were still live. The judgment language treats Great House Farm as one holding. It had not been one holding on the register. On the family’s case it had not been one holding since the 1877 split: Parcel A (house, buildings, garden/yard and about 10 acres, the Thomas/Williams line) and Parcel B (the eastern fields retained by Bute and later WGR/BP).
2 February 1987: application to amalgamate the two titles. WA240304 was then closed and registration continued under WA231076. That is the merge. It was made after the 1986 ruling and before the Court of Appeal gave judgment on 31 July 1987.
So 1983 is silent first registration of a second title while Mary was still in Parcel A, or had only just died. 1987 is the administrative merger, carried out while the appeal was still open.
This was not a dispute about a single land parcel that BP already owned. Mary was on Parcel A, which the family █████ she owned, with occupation on that house parcel running in the family from at least 1667. BP, and WGR before it from 1949, were the neighbouring interest on Parcel B. From 1949 onwards the family’s case is that those neighbours ran a decades-long series of tenancy offers, “whole farm” wording, possession orders and the 1974 letters to make her occupation of her own parcel look permissive, and to make both parcels look like one estate they had acquired. They never produced a conveyance of Parcel A. What they had was an unfounded claim that her occupancy was permissive.
Please treat any earlier letter from me that said the titles merged in 1983 as corrected by this email. The dates that matter are:
1982/83 — first registration of two titles, without the occupier being heard;
24 July 1986 — first-instance judgment describing one farm while two titles still stood;
2 February 1987 — amalgamation, before the appeal ended;
31 July 1987 — Court of Appeal.
Yours faithfully,

Requester

Annwyl Requester,

Diolch yn fawr am eich ymholiadau o 8, 15, 17 ac 20 Medi. Fel y awgrymir yn eich e-bost o 20 Medi, gwnaf ateb eich ymholiadau gyda’i gilydd.

Fel y dwedir yn fy e-byst o 28 Mai , 10 Mehefin, a 11 Mehefin, nid oes unrhyw lythyrau na chofnodion ynglŷn â’r safle hon, sef Fferm Tŷ Mawr, Llandochau Fach, yn ein ffeiliau cofrestredig, sef yr unig gofnodion ymgyrchol rydem eu cadw yn y tymor hir. Nid oes unrhyw gofnodion wedi dod i’r amlwg yn ystod y cyfnod ers hynny. Yn sgil hynny, yr unig wybodaeth sydd gennem ynglŷn â’r safle, gan gynnwys ei dymchwel, yw’r cofnodion yn ein harchif, sef Cofnod Henebion Cenedlaethol Cymru. Gellir gweld rhestr lawn ohonynt yma: https://coflein.gov.uk/en/sites/20182/archives. Ynglŷn ag awyrluniau, oherwydd cymhlethdod y casgliad hwn, byddai rhaid talu ar gyfer y chwiliadau hyn (gwelir y rhestr brisiau, a atodir, ar gyfer manylion). Petasai awyrluniau sydd yn cynnwys y safle yn bodoli, y mae’n debygol y byddent yn awyrluniau fertigol wedi’u tynnu o uchder uchel fel rhan o waith arolwg y tirlun arferol ac nid fyddent yn canolbwyntio ar y safle, na ei ddangos yn fanwl.

Ynglŷn â’ch ymholiad ynglŷn â’r arwisg a darganfuwyd yn ystod y bedwaredd ganrif ar bymtheg hwyr, nid oes sylw arno yn yr adroddiad gan Richard Suggett heb ei chyhoeddi, sef Rhif Archif 6048945 (https://coflein.gov.uk/en/archives/6048945). Gyda llaw, mae rhan fwyaf o’r cofnod hon wedi’i thanysgrifennu fel disgrifiad y safle gan Heneb, GGAT02038s (https://archwilio.org.uk/her/chi3/report/page.php?watprn=GGAT02038s&dbname=ggat&tbname=core&sessid=CHI4nj4fn3q&queryid=Q383581001790598378). Yr wyf yn gynnwys eu disgrifiad isod, wedi’i gwirio er mwyn adlewyrchu y testun gwreiddiol:
‘Great House Farmhouse and barn formed an attractive group, built of local lias limestone, and occupied an historic site next to the parish church. Finds of medieval ironwork and pottery have been reported from the site. Great House was the chief freehold farm of the parish and was occupied by the Vaughan's, a minor gentry family, from the mid C16 until the latter part of the C18. Several memorial inscriptions relating to the family are preserved in the church and churchyard. In the early C19 the freehold was acquired by the Bute Estate and the manorial courts for Llandough and Leckwith were held in Great House.

‘Externally both farmhouse and barn appeared to be of nineteenth-century date. Internally, however, surviving vernacular detail- a blocked stone fireplace stair and agee-stopped beams- suggested a seventeenth-century date for the house. The ground floor of the house was surveyed in unusual circumstances in 1974 by H.J.T. Much detail was then concealed and it was not possible to examine the first floor and roof trusses. The house remained partially recorded because of problems of access created by an ownership dispute. The house and farm buildings were suddenly and completely demolished by B.P. Properties Ltd. on 6th December 1988 amid considerable local controversy.

‘The plan of Great House was not published in the Inventory of Farmhouses & Cottages because of the incompleteness of the available information but it was classified as a sub-medieval house of direct-entry type (site no. 425). However, certain features suggested that the core of the house may have been medieval. The clearly-defined cross-passage end-chimney plan with masonry partitions and external wall batter (on the unreconstructed N side) had clear affinities with Brynwell, a medieval farmhouse in the neighbouring parish of Leckwith, Brynwell was built as a direct-entry, end-chimney, storeyed pre-Reformation house (Inventory, pp.187, 192). Brynwell, like Great House, was modernised in the C19th by the Bute Estate but the medieval date of the house is clearly shown by a small first-floor cusped-head window and the remodelled roof trusses. Unfortunately it was not possible to examine the fabric of Great House before the demolition of the house. Examination of the rubble brought to light no new features except an ogee-stopped beam with torus, a form of decoration that is not particularly common in Glamorgan (Inventory, Map 50).’

Er hynny, y mae dau gofnod sydd yn cyfeirio at ddarganfod yr arwisg, sef Rhif Archif 6048942 (https://coflein.gov.uk/en/archives/6048942), le y nodir ‘At one time it was reputed to be the stable of a Castle, which could be verified by the finding of the remains of a soldier in armour, his horse, lance and small shield under the dining room floor’, a Rhif Archif 6048944 (https://coflein.gov.uk/en/archives/6048944), sef erthygl o’r Daily Telegraph, 16 Ebrill 1974, le y nodir ‘Its history has never been fully chronicled but a theory that it was originally a coaching house near a Castle was supported by the discovery benieth the dining room floor in about 1870 of the remains of a soldier in armour, his horse, a lance and shield’. Gyda llaw, canys sefydlwyd y CBHC ac Amgueddfa Cymru yn yr ugeinfed ganrif gynnar a darganfuwyd yr arwisg yn y bedwaredd ganrif ar bymtheg, mae’n annhebyg y byddai’r Comisiwn Brenhinol yn rhan o rodiad yr arfwisg i’r Amgueddfa.

Gellir archebu sganiau'r tri chofnod hyn gan ddefnyddio’r ffurflen archebu a atodir. Wrth i ni hepgor ffioedd ar gyfer archebion bychain (llai na pum sgan cyfraniad ymchwil),  y mae’n debygol byddai darparir yr archeb hon am ddim.

Ynglŷn â’ch ymholiad ynglŷn â’r cofnodion Rhifau Archif 6364275 (https://coflein.gov.uk/en/archives/6364275)  a 6364276 (https://coflein.gov.uk/en/archives/6364276), yr wyf wedi ymgynghori’r ddau. Gallaf gadarnhau y mae’r ddau yn berthnasol i’r ddau safle y adnabyddir yn ein catalog archif, sef Tŷ Mawr, Tresimwn, a █████, Fynwy, ac nid Tŷ Mawr, Llandochau Fach.

Ynglŷn â’ch ymholiadau o 11 Mehefin, fel y dwedir uchod, nid oes unrhyw lythyrau na chofnodion ynglŷn â’r safle hon, sef Fferm Tŷ Mawr, Llandochau Fach, yn ein ffeiliau cofrestredig, sef yr unig gofnodion ymgyrchol rydem eu cadw yn y tymor hir. Nid ydy unrhyw gofnodion wedi dod yn amlwg yn ystod y cyfnod ers hynny. Er hynny, y mae’n amlwg bod aelod o’n tîm arolwg, sef Richard Suggett, wedi ymweld â’r safle yn fyr ar ôl ei dymchwel yn fis Rhagfyr 1988 (sef cynnwys y cofnod Rhif Archif 6048945), ond nid chofnodir rheswm yr ymweliad hwn.

Ynglŷn â’ch ymholiadau bellach o 20 Medi, fel y dwedir uchod, nid oes unrhyw lythyrau na chofnodion ynglŷn â’r safle hon, sef Fferm Tŷ Mawr, Llandochau Fach, yn ein ffeiliau cofrestredig, sef yr unig gofnodion ymgyrchol rydem eu cadw yn y tymor hir. Canys hynny, nid oes gennem lythyrau na chofnodion ynglŷn â’r llythyrau rhwng ‘C.N. Johns a Mrs Buckler, Great House Farm’, fel y dwedais yn fy e-bost o 10 Mehefin, na unrhyw amgylchiadau eraill ynglŷn â dymchwel y safle.

Y mae’r rhifau cofnodion a nodir yn eich e-bost o 20 Medi, sef NA/GL/88/49 a NA/GL/89/208 yn edrych yn debyg at rifau cofnodion derbyniadau. Yr unig gofnod a dderbynid fel rhan o NA/GL/89/208, ar ôl ein cofnodion, oedd Rhif Archif 6048941 (https://coflein.gov.uk/en/archives/6048941). Gyda llaw, mae’r cofnod hon wedi cael ei gynnwys yn yr adroddiad GGAT ‘Land at Great House Farm, Llandough. An Archaeological Assessment’ (1990), sef Rhif Archif 6524751 (https://coflein.gov.uk/en/archives/6524751). Fel y dwedais yn fy e-bost o 28 Mai, gellir gweld copi digidol o’r adroddiad hon yma: https://www.walesher1974.org/her/app/php/herumd.php?group=GGAT&level=3&docid=301361628.

Fel y sefydlir nid oes gennem gofnodion ynglŷn â’r mater hon heblaw am y rhai sydd yn ein harchif, sydd ar gael i’r cyhoedd trwy ein Gwasanaeth Ymholiadau cyhoeddus, mi fydd pob ymholiad pellach ynglŷn â’r mater hon yn cael ei thrin fel ymholiad cyhoeddus. Yr eiddoch yn gywir,

> 1. A full contents list or file schedule for **NA/GL/88/49** and **NA/GL/89/208**, itemising every document on each file, whether or not the documents themselves are disclosed.
> 2. Copies of all documents on those two files.
> 3. **The file cover, front sheet or wrapper of each file**, and any enclosure list, loans register, issue slip, reader-request record or file-tracking entry attached to or kept for them.
> 4. Every record concerning the **C. N. Johns / Mrs Buckler correspondence** recorded as lost since 1986/87: any surviving copy, draft, extract, summary, index entry or catalogue stub; any contemporaneous or later note of its loss; any record of a search for it; any record of who consulted, borrowed or handled the file between 1 January 1985 and 31 December 1988; and any internal or external correspondence about its absence. > 5. The Commission's **retention and disposal schedule** applicable to site files and correspondence files in the 1980s and today, and confirmation whether any records relating to this site have been destroyed under it, and if so when and under what authority.
> 6. Whether the files listed above have been **reviewed for transfer to, or retention from, The National Archives or the Glamorgan Archives**, and the outcome of any such review.
> 7. All **Inventory working papers, drafts, card-index entries and record cards** for the site, including those for Glamorgan Inventory site 425.
> 8. All **photographs** of the site in any format — prints, negatives, transparencies, digital images, and any oblique or vertical aerial coverage of Llandough showing the farm at any date — whether or not catalogued, with their catalogue entries. Given Suggett's 1988 note that there is apparently no photographic record, **please state expressly whether the Commission holds none**, and whether any images sit within RCS2/1/1777 or in uncatalogued Emergency Recording material.
> 9. Confirmation, from the location plan, map copies and photographs inside **RCS2/1/1777**, whether that bundle is Bonvilston or Llandough. If Llandough, please re-link it to NPRN 20182 and supply a contents list and copies. Please also check adjacent case **RCS2/1/1776**. *(This is my request of 15 September, restated here for completeness only — it stands on its own date.)*
> 10. Any record of a site visit, watching brief, recording exercise or emergency recording carried out or considered before, during or after the demolition; any notification of the proposed demolition, from whom and on what date; and any decision **not** to record the building together with the reasons recorded for it. The building was not listed — Cadw inspected on 29 July 1988 and did not list it — so I make no assumption that the Commission was entitled to notice. What I would like to know is what the Commission's own criteria for initiating Emergency Recording were at the time, and whether this site was considered against them. Contemporary reports of 3 December 1988 stated that Cadw was considering emergency listing and that discussion with the Commission was being arranged. The house came down three days later.
> 11. The **1974 survey by H. J. Thomas**, his site notes of 26 April 1974 and 12 December 1988, and any measured drawings, sketches, plans or elevations, published or unpublished.
> 12. **R. F. Suggett's December 1988 records in full** — every page, card, continuation sheet, annotation and enclosure — not only the passages concerning the c.1880 find.
> 13. Any record of the source of the statement that the c.1880 ironwork "is held by the National Museum of Wales", and any later file that confirms, corrects or withdraws that attribution.
> 14. All correspondence between the Commission and any of the following concerning this site, 1970–1995: Cadw or the Welsh Office; the Glamorgan-Gwent Archaeological Trust; Vale of Glamorgan Borough Council; BP Properties Limited or its agents, including Debenham Tewson & Chinnocks; Persimmon Homes (Wales) Limited; Ideal Homes Wales Limited; Amgueddfa Cymru; any Member of Parliament; and any member of my family.

If any item is held elsewhere — The National Archives, Glamorgan Archives, Cadw, Heneb or Amgueddfa Cymru — please name the body and reference so I can apply there directly, which I will.
>
> Finally, so that it is on record from the outset rather than raised later: please let me have the name and contact details of the officer responsible for information rights at the Commission, and confirmation of the internal review procedure, so that I know where to direct any review request if one becomes necessary.

Thank you for your email of the 28/09/26 in relation to your request for an
internal review into the way the department handled your request for
information under reference: 26FOI 103.

Your request is being handled under the Freedom of Information Act 2000
(FOIA).



We will endeavour to inform you of the outcome of your internal review no
later than the 26/10/26.



The review of your request will consist of an analysis of the handling of
your request by an independent official who was not involved in handling
your original request. If the original decision is overturned, the request
will be re-visited and any information, if held, released to you, entirely
or in part. If the original decision is upheld, you will receive a letter
from the Freedom of Information team detailing the reasons why we are
unable to provide the requested information.

If on receipt of our response you are still not satisfied, you can make a
further appeal to the Information Commissioner. You can write to the
Information Commissioner at:
Information Commissioner
Wycliffe House
Water Lane
Wilmslow
Cheshire
SK9 5AFFurther information about the role of the Information Commissioner
and the appeals process can be found at www.ico.org.uk

If you wish to discuss this, please contact the Freedom of Information

Yours sincerely,


Freedom of Information Team

> Freedom of Information Team

> Dear Sir or Madam,
>
> Request for Internal Review — 26FOI 103 — response dated 22 September 2026
> Requester: Requester
>
> I request an internal review of the handling and substance of 26FOI 103.
>
> This is an FOI review only. I am not asking the Wales Office to
> determine title, to reopen BP Properties Ltd v Buckler, or to adopt
> any party's case on the land. I am asking whether the letter of 22
> September 2026 answered the request that was made, and whether the
> search described in it was adequate.
>
> A. What is already on this file
>
> 1. 29 August 2026 — I asked the Wales Office for recorded information
> about Great House Farm. Your letter of 22 September quotes the request
> as five points. I adopt that quotation. The points were:
>
> - records of any communication or outreach between Cadw, or its
> predecessor functions, and the Office of the Secretary of State for
> Wales / Welsh Office concerning Great House Farm during July–December
> 1988;
> - records of any recommendation, briefing, submission, notification or
> formal appeal concerning the protection or listing of Great House Farm
> submitted to the Secretary of State;
> - records of any communications with the occupiers and owners of the
> property before the refusal decision of 5 December 1988;
> - any surviving destruction, disposal, transfer or accession
> documentation relating to the Great House Farm 1988 assessment file,
> including certificates, dockets, lists, database entries, retention
> schedules, disposal authorities or other contemporaneous records held
> by the Welsh Office, its predecessors, Cadw, or any repository to
> which relevant records were transferred;
> - information regarding a decision made in relation to Great House
> Farm in 1988, including the evidence that was used to support that
> decision.
>
> 2. 8 September 2026 — acknowledgement from NIO FOI (█████),
> recording the request date as 29/08/26. It named no officer and
> described no search.
>
> 3. 22 September 2026 — covering email from the same NIO FOI mailbox,
> attaching “26FOI 103 - Buckler - Response.pdf”. The covering email
> contained no substance. The letter is signed Freedom of Information
> Team, Wales Office, and directs any review to
> █████.
>
> This review is within the two calendar months stated in that letter.
> The deadline you gave is 22 November 2026.
>
> B. What the letter actually █████, and what it does not
>
> The operative paragraph is this:
>
> “We have carried out a search of our digital records and have
> determined that the Wales Office does not hold the information
> requested. Any paper files previously held by the former Welsh Office
> relating to this matter would have been transferred to the National
> Assembly for Wales in 1999, and subsequently to the Welsh Government
> in 2007.”
>
> That paragraph does not answer the request. The gaps are these.
>
> 1. Digital records only. The letter █████ a search of digital records.
> It does not say that paper, microfilm, card indexes, transfer lists,
> accession registers, or destruction schedules were searched. A 1988
> Welsh Office file is a paper file. A search confined to current
> digital holdings cannot find it, and cannot find the transfer or
> destruction docket that the fourth bullet asked for.
>
> 2. “Would have been transferred” is not a search result. It is an
> assumption about devolution. It is not a statement that a transfer
> list was consulted, that a file for this house appears on that list,
> or that the file was received in Cardiff. “Would have been” covers
> three different outcomes: transferred, destroyed, or still here under
> another description. The letter does not distinguish them.
>
> 3. The fourth bullet asked for the transfer, disposal and accession
> records themselves. Those records, if they exist, are Wales Office
> records of what left the building. They are not the assessment file.
> Pointing me to the Welsh Government does not answer a request for the
> docket, the list, the database entry or the disposal authority. Those
> may still be held here even if the file went to Cardiff. The letter
> does not say they were searched for.
>
> 4. The five bullets are not answered one by one. There is no finding
> on communications with Cadw; no finding on any briefing or appeal to
> the Secretary of State; no finding on communications with occupiers
> and owners before 5 December 1988; no finding on the evidence said to
> have supported a 1988 decision. A single sentence that digital records
> do not hold “the information requested” does not show that each limb
> was searched.
>
> 5. The letter uses “the refusal decision of 5 December 1988” only
> because I used it. It does not say whether that decision is
> recognised, whether a file for it was identified, or whether the
> decision is one of the papers “which would have been transferred”.
> Silence on a dated decision is not a not-held finding.
>
> 6. “You may therefore wish” is not section 16 advice. Section 16
> requires advice and assistance so far as reasonable. A reasonable
> step, where the department asserts a transfer, is to give the
> receiving body's file reference, the date of transfer, and the series.
> None is given. If the intention was section 21 (information reasonably
> accessible elsewhere), that exemption is not named, and the conditions
> are not addressed. A suggestion that I write to
> █████ is not a section 21 notice.
>
> 7. “Does not hold” is stated as a conclusion. The search described
> cannot support it. A not-held finding under section 1 requires a
> search capable of finding the information. A search of digital
> records, plus an assumption about 1999, is not that search.
>
> 8. The request was answered from a Northern Ireland Office mailbox.
> The letter is in the name of the Wales Office. The review must be of
> the Wales Office search. Please confirm it will not be taken by the
> person who signed the 22 September letter.
>
> C. What the reviewing officer is asked to determine
>
> 1. What was searched, by name: digital systems, paper series, transfer
> lists, accession registers, destruction schedules, Gwydyr House
> holdings, and any index of files passed to the National Assembly in
> 1999 or to the Welsh Government in 2007. If a location was not
> searched, say so.
>
> 2. For each of the five bullets, a separate finding: held, not held
> after the searches at (1), transferred (with date, recipient and
> reference), or destroyed (with date and disposal authority).
>
> 3. Whether any transfer, disposal or accession record relating to a
> Great House Farm 1988 assessment file is held by this department, as
> distinct from the assessment file itself.
>
> 4. Whether any record of a decision on or about 5 December 1988, or of
> communications with the occupiers or owners before that date, was
> identified even as an index entry.
>
> 5. If information is held and is not to be disclosed, a section 17
> notice naming the exemption. Do not replace that notice with a
> referral.
>
> 6. If the review maintains that the file went to Cardiff, the transfer
> reference. Without it, the referral is an assertion.
>
> D. Scope, so the review is not narrowed again
>
> The window is July–December 1988. Possession of Great House Farm / Tŷ
> Mawr, Llandough, adjoining St Dochdwy's, was taken on 29 November
> 1988. Demolition of the farmhouse began on 6 December 1988. The
> refusal date in the request is 5 December 1988. Those dates fix the
> search. They do not ask you to decide the land.
>
> I have made a parallel request to the Welsh Government, following the
> referral. That does not discharge 26FOI 103. A file can have been
> transferred and the transfer docket can still be here. Both questions
> were asked. Only one was gestured at.
>
> E. Why these records are in scope, without asking you to decide title
>
> The public index is https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/
>
> The investigation distinguishes Parcel A (farmhouse, garden, buildings
> and yard — the family's maintained freehold interest out of the Bute
> estate) from Parcel B (eastern fields). Later papers use “whole farm”.
> BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 decided possession,
> limitation and the October 1974 letters. It did not decide the
> documentary root of Parcel A. Whether the Secretary of State or Cadw
> looked at this house in the week it was refused and pulled down is a
> records question. It is not a request that you adopt the family's
> case.
>
> F. Preservation
>
> Please preserve any record that may fall within 26FOI 103 while this
> review is open, including transfer lists, destruction schedules and
> anything due for routine disposal. Do not transfer or destroy in-scope
> material without a written receipt that can be disclosed on the
> review.
>
> G. Reservation
>
> This letter does not waive any position on title, registration,
> concealment, limitation, or any later reopening. It is an internal
> review under the Freedom of Information Act 2000. It is not a claim
> form and is not service of proceedings.
>
> Please acknowledge receipt, give the review reference, and state the
> date by which the review will be completed. ICO guidance is that an
> internal review should normally be completed within 20 working days.
>
> Yours faithfully,
>
> Requester 
> █████
>

records.transcript:
Dear Adam,

Thank you for your detailed response of 29 September (RC26-0375). It is
particularly helpful to have your confirmation that Archive 6048945 records
Richard Suggett's visit to the site after its demolition in December 1988,
and for identifying Archives 6048941, 6048942 and 6048944.

I have considered your response alongside the Commission's catalogue
entries and the other records now available. Before any of the outstanding
September requests are treated as concluded, I need to clarify one
distinction.

You state (as in your emails of 28 May, 10 June and 11 June) that there are
no letters or records concerning Tŷ Mawr Farm, Llandough, in the
Commission's registered files, which you describe as the only campaign
records kept in the long term.

I note that answer. My requests were not confined to registered campaign
files. They concern recorded information held by the Commission relating to
the site, including records which your own archive identifies as existing,
lost, received or created in connection with it.

I am happy for the points below to be answered in whatever order is most
convenient, provided the FOIA/EIR status and original dates of the
September requests are preserved. Where a point has already been answered
in full, a short confirmation that nothing further is held will suffice; I
do not wish the Commission to repeat itself.

1. Scope of the search

Please confirm whether the search has extended beyond registered files to
other relevant NMRW collections and systems, including (where applicable):

- Inventory working papers, drafts, record cards and historic index cards;
- field and survey notes;
- measured drawings, sketches, plans and elevations;
- maps and plan collections;
- photographic collections, negatives and indexes;
- vertical and oblique aerial photography and its indexes;
- grey literature and unpublished reports;
- special, personal or specialist collections;
- background records;
- historic administrative records;
- digital and legacy catalogue systems;
- accession and deposit records;
- transfer, withdrawal, de-accession or disposal records; and
- uncatalogued or separately catalogued material reasonably capable of
containing information about the site.

Please also confirm whether the search used the principal known identifiers
and variants, including:

Great House Farm; Great House; Tŷ Mawr; Ty Mawr Farm; Llandough;
Llandochau; Llandough-juxta-Penarth; NPRN 20182; ST 1681 7331; ST16707335;
GGAT02038s; Inventory site 425; NA/GL/88/49; NA/GL/89/208; RCS2/1/1777;
RCS2/1/1776; 6048941; 6048942; 6048944; 6048945; C.N. Johns; CN Johns; and
Mrs Buckler.

If any of the categories above were not searched, a simple statement to
that effect is sufficient.

2. The lost C.N. Johns / Mrs Buckler correspondence

The surviving Suggett record (Archive 6048945) identifies correspondence
between C.N. Johns and Mrs Buckler as having been lost from the file since
1986/87.

Your response establishes that the correspondence itself cannot now be
located. Please therefore confirm whether the Commission has also searched
for any residual records about that correspondence, including:

- a file cover or wrapper;
- enclosure or contents list;
- accession or receipt entry;
- issue, loan or handling record;
- reader-request record;
- catalogue or index card;
- duplicate copy;
- draft, extract or summary;
- contemporary note concerning its absence;
- later note concerning its loss;
- correspondence concerning its loss;
- transfer or return record; or
- any other record identifying when or how the correspondence ceased to be
with the file.

If none of those records exists, please say so expressly. The question is
no longer simply whether the correspondence survives, but whether the
surviving archive contains any documentary trace of its provenance and
disappearance.

3. Archive 6048945

Please provide the complete surviving contents of Archive 6048945 (every
page, card, continuation sheet, annotation and enclosure).

Please also confirm whether 6048945 is a complete standalone record, part
of a larger file or collection, an extract separated from a parent record,
or linked in any catalogue, accession or administrative system to other
records concerning Great House Farm/Tŷ Mawr.

You have confirmed that Suggett visited the site after demolition. Please
also confirm whether there is any surviving record giving the date or
purpose of that visit beyond the description currently catalogued, or any
associated site note, field sheet, photograph, sketch or correspondence.

4. NA/GL/88/49 and NA/GL/89/208

Thank you for explaining the relationship between those admission
references and Archives 6048945 and 6048941.

Please confirm whether the Commission retains any admission register entry,
receipt, accession sheet, contents list, file wrapper, box/listing record,
catalogue amendment, transfer record or other metadata showing what was
originally received under NA/GL/88/49 and NA/GL/89/208.

In particular, if 6048941 is the only surviving record received under
NA/GL/89/208, please confirm whether that conclusion comes from an original
admission record or simply from what is currently visible in the catalogue.

5. RCS2/1/1777 and RCS2/1/1776

I appreciate the clarification concerning Archive Numbers 6364275 and
6364276.

The separate question concerning RCS2/1/1777 remains open. Please confirm
whether the contents of RCS2/1/1777 have actually been inspected (including
location plan, photographs, captions and associated recording material)
sufficiently to establish whether the site is Bonvilston or Llandough.

If it is Bonvilston, I will record that as resolved. If it is Llandough,
please explain whether the catalogue has been or will be corrected or
linked to NPRN 20182, and provide the contents and copies requested earlier.

Please also confirm whether RCS2/1/1776 has been checked for the same
reason.

6. Photographs and aerial photography

I note your explanation that searching the aerial collection may involve a
charge.

Before deciding whether to commission a paid search, please tell me what
the Commission's existing indexes or catalogue systems establish about
aerial coverage of the relevant location:

- Is there any aerial coverage containing the site?
- Is there any vertical or oblique coverage for the relevant period?
- Is there any photograph taken during or after the demolition?
- Are there catalogue entries for photographs which are no longer held?
- Does the Commission have any image connected to NPRN 20182 which is not
presently visible on Coflein?

This is relevant to Suggett's statement that there was apparently no
photographic record of the site. I would like to distinguish “Suggett could
identify no photographic record at the time” from “the Commission has
searched its photographic collections and holds no photograph of the site”.
A nil return following a defined search of the photographic and aerial
indexes would itself be a useful result.

7. The 1974 survey and the ownership dispute

Your quotation of Archive 6048945 now establishes (as a matter of the
Commission's own file) that the house remained partially recorded because
of problems created by an ownership dispute. That point is therefore
settled.

Please confirm whether the Commission holds anything beyond the material
already visible on Coflein concerning:

- H.J. Thomas's 26 April 1974 survey;
- the 1974 site notes;
- the 12 December 1988 additions to the plan;
- measured drawings;
- field notes;
- correspondence concerning access; or
- any decision about what could or could not be recorded because of the
ownership dispute.

I am not asking the Commission to adjudicate the ownership dispute. I am
seeking only to establish what recording opportunities existed and what
records were actually made. (For context, the Commission's post-demolition
addition to the 1974 plan on 12 December 1988 is the only institutional
building-recording event identified in the immediate aftermath of the
demolition.)

8. Transfers, retention and disposal

Please confirm whether any records concerning Great House Farm/Tŷ Mawr were
ever transferred to another repository, received from another repository,
returned to a depositor, withdrawn, de-accessioned, destroyed, or otherwise
removed from the Commission's custody. Where such an event occurred, please
provide the recorded date, description, authority/reference and destination
where held.

In particular, please confirm whether relevant material was ever
transferred to or received from Cadw/Welsh Office/Welsh Government,
Glamorgan Archives, The National Archives, Amgueddfa Cymru, GGAT/Heneb or
another institution. (I note that the public HER entry GGAT02038s now
incorporates material derived from the Commission's 1988 records; any
residual administrative link or transfer record relating to that would be
useful.)

9. The nineteenth-century deposit

Thank you for identifying Archives 6048942 and 6048944.

I am not asking the Commission to endorse the historical account. I would
like the provenance of the RCAHMW record established, so far as it can be:

- what source was used to create Archive 6048942;
- whether that source was contemporary, retrospective or copied from
another publication;
- whether RCAHMW ever examined the █████ objects itself;
- whether any accession, transfer or correspondence record connected the
account with Amgueddfa Cymru; and
- whether the attribution that material was held by the National Museum of
Wales appears elsewhere in the Commission's records.

If the Commission has no such provenance information, please say so. (For
completeness, Amgueddfa Cymru has separately stated that it holds no record
of such an acquisition; I raise the point only to establish the documentary
trail within the Commission's own holdings.)

10. The demolition sequence

Your confirmation that Suggett visited after demolition makes the following
question particularly important.

Please confirm whether the Commission holds any record of notification of
the proposed demolition, notification during the demolition, a request for
(or consideration of, or decision not to undertake) emergency recording, a
site visit before, during or immediately after demolition, or contact with
Cadw, GGAT, the relevant local authority, BP Properties or its agents, or
Mrs Buckler or any other family member.

I am aware that the Commission may not have been under a statutory duty to
receive notice merely because the building was unlisted. I am not assuming
otherwise. The question is simply whether any such recorded information
exists. The Commission's own addition to the plan on 12 December 1988 is
the only institutional recording event so far identified in the immediate
post-demolition period; any residual notes or correspondence from that
visit would therefore be of particular value.

11. Search statement

Because the principal issue is now the distinction between “not in the
registered files” and “not held anywhere by the Commission”, I would be
grateful for a short factual search statement identifying:

- which physical record series were searched;
- which electronic/catalogue systems were searched;
- the principal names, site identifiers or reference numbers used;
- whether relevant archive staff or custodians were consulted; and
- whether any potentially relevant material was excluded because it was
uncatalogued, separately indexed, deposited or otherwise outside the
registered-file series.

A concise factual description is sufficient; I am not asking for an
elaborate report.

12. Statutory status

Finally, I do not want the distinction between the Commission's public
enquiry/research service and its statutory information-rights function to
become blurred.

My requests of 8, 15, 17 and 20 September 2026 remain as made. I am content
for the Commission to answer them together where that is administratively
easier, but I am not withdrawing them or converting them into paid research
enquiries.

Please therefore confirm:

1. which request or requests your present email is intended to answer;
2. whether each outstanding request remains open;
3. whether your present email is intended to constitute a formal FOIA/EIR
response;
4. where you say information is not held, the scope of the search
supporting that conclusion;
5. where information is being withheld rather than not held, the relevant
statutory basis; and
6. the applicable internal-review procedure and the name/contact details of
the officer responsible for information rights.

I appreciate the distinction you have drawn between material the Commission
currently holds and material which may once have existed. That distinction
is precisely why I am trying to establish the documentary chain carefully
rather than draw conclusions from gaps in the archive.

I am deliberately approaching this as a records-reconstruction exercise. I
am not asking the Commission to reach a conclusion about ownership, the
legality of the demolition, or the conduct of any person or institution.

My aim is to establish what records were created, what survives, what
entered or left the Commission's custody, what was transferred or disposed
of, what cannot now be located, and what searches have actually been
undertaken.

Thank you again for your assistance. I would be grateful if the outstanding
September requests could remain open while these points of clarification
are addressed.

Regards,

Requester

Information Governance Team,

*Case Ref 00210772 — internal review requested 7 July 2026*

Thank you for your email of 11 September. You said that you would try to
update me by the end of the following week with a clearer timeframe. I have
not received that update.

Under regulation 11(4) of the Environmental Information Regulations 2004,
an internal review should be completed as soon as possible and no later
than 40 working days after receipt of the request for reconsideration. On
my calculation, that period expired on 2 September 2026. The review is
therefore now overdue.

I appreciate that further historical documentation has been located and
that you may need to consult third parties. I am not asking you to
compromise any proper consultation process. However, I ask that you now
provide the following by *Tuesday 6 October 2026*:

   1.

   *A firm date* by which the completed internal review decision will be
   issued.
   2.

   *A non-disclosive description of the further documentation located*,
   including, so far as presently known:
   - its approximate date or date range;
      - who created or supplied it;
      - how it came into the Council's possession; and
      - approximately how many documents are involved.

   I am asking for a description of the material and its provenance, rather
   than disclosure of its substantive contents.
   3.

   *Confirmation that the newly located documentation is being preserved in
   its present form*, without alteration, destruction or disposal, while
   the internal review and any subsequent complaint to the Information
   Commissioner remain outstanding.
   4.

   *Release now of any material that can properly be disclosed without
   awaiting third-party consultation*, where the Council has already
   established that no exemption or other restriction prevents disclosure.

If I do not receive a substantive response by *6 October 2026*, I will
refer the continuing delay to the Information Commissioner's Office without
further notice.

Regards,

Requester

Dr Wigley / Cadw Complaints Manager,

This is not a new complaint and not a chase. It is notice for the stage-one
complaint already opened under ticket #628635887: complaint of 17 September
2026, re-served on 20 September after delivery to █████ was
rejected, with a supplement sent on 22 September.

The complaint is that Cadw’s 1988 assessment of Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr),
Llandough-juxta-Penarth (approximately ST 1681 7331; later HER GGAT02038s),
did not adequately address the historic fabric, archaeological context and
information then available, and that the building was demolished in
December 1988 before any listing protection was secured.

I am not asking Cadw to determine title. I am asking Cadw to answer for its
own role, decisions and professional handling of the 1988 assessment.

What I seek from this complaint, if Cadw is willing to resolve it without
referral to the Public Services Ombudsman for Wales, is:

1. A written stage-one decision on whether Cadw’s 1988 assessment was
adequate having regard to the material then available and the criteria and
process applicable at the time, including the relevant 1979 GGAT excavation
record concerning the Roman villa and associated early-medieval archaeology
on land formerly within the farm holding.

2. If Cadw concludes that the assessment was inadequate, a written
acknowledgement of that finding, confined to Cadw’s own role and without
determination of title or third-party liability.

3. Cadw’s confirmation of whether it will ask Heneb to review HER entry

This is a short supplement to my letter of 20 September 2026 on the
historic environment record for Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough (NPRN

2. The HM Land Registry letter forwarded by the constituency MP was dated
18 September 2026, not “yesterday”. On 27 September I wrote separately to

about titles WA231076 and WA240304. That correction is not a request to you.

published page now states that Historic Environment Records in Wales:
Compilation and Use (2017) is issued as statutory guidance under section
196 of the 2023 Act. What I still need is confirmation whether that 2017
text has been substantively reviewed since sections 194 to 196 came into
force on 4 November 2024, and the date on which the current guidance was
issued under section 196 and laid before Senedd Cymru. I would also be

classification of records and the behaviour of the public interface.

the site to the separate 1994 excavation event, GGATE003875, which contains

From: Requester  
Sent: 22 September 2026 16:51
To: Wigley, Andy (LCC - Cadw)  
Cc: Complaints - Cwynion  ; Cadw Planning  
Subject: Supplement to complaint re-served 20 September 2026 — Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough

Dr Wigley,

This is a supplement to the complaint re-served on 20 September, not a chaser. I do not expect a reply before the stage-one response. It adds seven matters under the existing headings at section 7, and one addition to the outcomes at section 9, set out at the end.

The public interest is engaged alongside my family's. Great House Farm stood beside the Grade I church at Llandough, was recorded by the Royal Commission in 1974, sat within a known archaeological site, and was described in the post-demolition planning record as a "county treasure". I do not ask Cadw to treat the 1994 discoveries as knowledge it had in 1988. They show what was lost; the pre-1988 record is the measure of Cadw's process.

On my family's account and the contemporary press report, protection was being sought in the first days of December 1988 and the house was demolished almost immediately afterwards. I do not ask Cadw to determine responsibility for the demolition. The grievance is narrower: protection was sought at the critical moment, and Cadw cannot now show what it considered.

1. The adopted development plan (matter A)

The planning officer's report on application 89/01396/OUT records that the supporting information to Policy H.2 of the East Vale Local Plan "states that buildings on the site should be retained, however were unfortunately demolished a little while ago." I do not say this bound Cadw or required listing. I ask:
(a) was Cadw aware of it in December 1988;
(b) did the planning authority draw it to Cadw's attention; and
(c) if neither can be established, will Cadw say so expressly.

2. The search undertaken on 21 May (matters D and F)

Mr Weatherhead wrote that he had asked a colleague to search other paper files, "including the Welsh Office files", and would write again with the result, while fairly warning that some files had quite likely been destroyed. I have not received that letter. Please confirm whether the search was carried out, which series were searched, what was found, and whether Cadw regards the ATISN 27021 response of 11 June as its report of that search.

3. The meaning of "YYY" (matter J)

Cadw has given two accounts of the marking — that the buildings were "marginally below the bar for listing" (21 May) and that the building did not meet the criteria (10 July) — and one inference, that it did not meet the criteria "as it was not included on the list" (29 July). I ask for one settled meaning, the documentary source for it, and, if there is none, a statement to that effect.

4. The retention period (matter J)

Your email of 27 August said that no records of the historic retention arrangements are available, and that the three-year period is what current colleagues advised from their knowledge of the systems then in place. I ask only that the complaint response confirm expressly that this is an account of general practice, not evidence that the Great House Farm file was in fact destroyed after three years.

5. Professional archaeological knowledge of this site before December 1988 (matter C)

On 22 September 2026 Amgueddfa Cymru disclosed to me, under FOI 2026-032, its collections records for two accessions from this site. The first, 82.44H, is the material from the Glamorgan-Gwent Archaeological Trust's excavation of 1979 on land formerly part of Great House Farm, carried out in advance of housing development. The museum's records give the findspot as ST 168 733, the donor as Wales & West Housing Association Ltd, and the published report as Owen-John 1988. The accession runs to several hundred entries and includes Roman coins, samian, glass, a bone scabbard slide and querns, together with medieval pottery and ironwork.

This is not archaeology discovered after the event. By the time Cadw considered this building, the site had been professionally excavated, the finds had been accessioned by the national museum under a 1982 accession number, and the excavation report had been published. I therefore ask, as an addition to matter C:
(a) whether Cadw held, or had access to, the 1979 excavation record or its published report when it considered the buildings in 1988;
(b) whether that material was drawn to its attention by GGAT, the planning authority or the Royal Commission; and
(c) if neither can now be established, that Cadw say so in terms.

I do not say this material required the building to be listed. I say that the conclusion recorded in December 1988, that the site was not of sufficient archaeological interest, was reached against a professional record that already existed and is still held by the national museum today.

6. The National Museum attribution (matter H)

The GGAT assessment of August 1990, which Cadw supplied to me on 21 May, states that "it is likely that some medieval ironwork which is held by the National Museum of Wales was discovered under the rear wing c 1880 (RCAHMW 1988)."

The museum's disclosure allows that sentence to be tested, and the position is more precise than either of us has previously put it. The museum does hold medieval ironwork from this site — knife blades, arrowheads, a buckle and a pair of compasses within accession 82.44H — but as excavated material from 1979, not as an 1880 discovery beneath the rear wing. Its searches found no accession, donation or deposit answering the c.1880 provenance at all. The museum's own explanation, given in its disclosure, is that objects recorded as found at Church Farm, Llandough in 1858 and donated in 1963 under accession 63.24 "could well be the basis for such a local story/tradition".

I therefore no longer ask Cadw to accept that the attribution is uncorroborated in the round. I ask, more narrowly, whether Cadw holds anything supporting the c.1880 rear-wing provenance beyond the GGAT sentence it forwarded, and whether it will ask that the derived record note the museum's findings rather than continue to carry the 1880 attribution unqualified.

7. Correcting the record (matter H)

You directed me to Heneb as manager of the HER, which was reasonable. The only substantive reply I have had from Heneb is its statement of 22 May that it is not subject to FOI as a limited company; a schedule I sent on 19 September remains outstanding.

The museum's disclosure now gives a firm anchor for what the record should show. Accession 95.56H comprises the material from the Cotswold Archaeological Trust excavation of 1994, donated by Ideal Homes Wales Ltd, and its locality is recorded in the museum's own collections database as "Great House Farm Llandough" at ST 1681 7331 — the grid reference carried by the historic environment record for this site. That accession runs to several hundred sets of early medieval human remains from this ground.

As the statutory duty to keep historic environment records rests with the Welsh Ministers, I ask:
(a) which body is responsible for correcting an inaccurate or incomplete historic environment record;
(b) what Cadw's own role is where the record is managed by Heneb; and
(c) what Cadw will do if the entry for this site (GGAT02038s) is not corrected to reflect the 1979 and 1994 excavations and the accessions arising from them.

Correction to my letter of 20 September

I said █████  had rejected my correspondence on three occasions. Having checked properly, it rejected messages on at least eight occasions between January and September 2026: 23 January; 9 May (twice); 17 May; 10 August; 11 August; 29 August; and 17 September. Separate failures on 29 August and 17 September came from the retired address █████ . I correct this because I have asked Cadw to distinguish what is established from what is inferred, and the same standard applies to me.

Addition to the outcomes at section 9

6. A written acknowledgement that the 21 May undertaking was not reported on, and that Cadw's accounts of the 1988 assessment have varied.
7. A single statement of what can and cannot now be established about the 1988 decisions, which my family can rely on and cite.
8. That Cadw write to Heneb and the Royal Commission asking that their records for this site reflect that statement and the museum's accession records.
9. Consideration, under the Welsh Government complaints policy, of redress for the time and trouble my family has spent since May pursuing questions that Cadw's own records could not answer.

I am content to supply the museum's disclosure to Cadw if that would assist, and my offer of 20 September stands: any 1988 Cadw correspondence recovered from the Royal Commission or Heneb will be sent to you. I remain grateful for the courtesy you and your colleagues have shown me.

Yours sincerely,

Requester

records.transcript:
Dear Mr/Ms Rutter,

Further to my email of earlier today and your message of 29 September 2026.

I am writing to place further material and context before the Victim
Liaison Unit so that CPS Cymru-Wales has the information necessary to
identify any existing record or referral and, where appropriate, to ensure
that the material reaches the prosecutor or team responsible for
considering it.

I am not asking the CPS to determine the underlying civil title to the
property. The issue I am raising is whether the documentary history gives
rise to potential criminal offences, whether those matters warrant
investigation, and, if a private prosecution is subsequently instituted,
whether the circumstances are such that the Director's power under section
6(2) of the Prosecution of Offences Act 1985 should be considered.

1. Police engagement and current references

On 28 September 2026 I submitted a formal crime-recording request to South
Wales Police (█████), copied to Stephen Doughty
MP for constituency-record purposes only.

The request asks South Wales Police to record, or explain in writing why
they will not record, a report concerning suspected █████ and related
concealment in the creation and subsequent use of registered title to the
former Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough. It identifies, in particular,
the first-registration application for WA231076 dated 30 November 1982, the
application for WA240304 dated 23 February 1983, and matters arising from
the subsequent 1987 proceedings.

I also have a live Subject Access Request with South Wales Police
concerning the 1988 eviction and demolition and related personal data.

I previously reported suspected irregularities concerning the 1982
registration to HM Land Registry (reference 260202-5732372). Further HM
Land Registry enquiry references include 260929-6766714 and related
references generated in September 2026.

If a Report █████ reference is issued, I will provide it immediately. For
present purposes, I ask that the South Wales Police crime-recording request
and the HM Land Registry report of suspected registration irregularities be
treated as the principal current investigative references.

2. Documentary title sequence and suspected criminality

The public evidence index is available at:

https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/

The material assembled there identifies a documentary sequence which, in my
present assessment, raises questions as to whether the family's historic
proprietary interest in the farmhouse parcel was displaced through the use
of records, possession evidence and registration material relating to a
different or wider parcel, and whether subsequent registration and dealings
then relied upon that resulting title position.

For convenience, I refer on the website to this as the "synthetic title"
issue. That is a description of the documentary pattern I have identified,
rather than an assumption that criminal liability has already been
established.

The distinction is important because the 1987 Court of Appeal proceedings
concerned possession, limitation and the October 1974 correspondence. My
concern is that those proceedings did not determine the underlying
documentary root of title to the farmhouse parcel now represented by the
registered title history.

3. 1955 possession order and the neighbouring parcel

A further issue requiring examination is the relationship between the 1955
possession order and the land historically occupied and claimed by the
Williams/Buckler family.

My evidence indicates that the 1955 order related to a neighbouring parcel
rather than the family's core farmhouse holding. I am concerned that
subsequent possession and development activity may nevertheless have
treated that order, or the associated possession history, as extending to
land outside the parcel to which it actually related.

Recent excavation and works on the former family land make this a live
evidential issue. I ask that the underlying order, plans, descriptions and
subsequent land use be considered against the documentary title sequence
rather than assuming that the parcels were identical.

4. Possible loss or destruction of relevant records

I hold dated photographs concerning works which removed a commemorative
tree planted by my great-grandfather on or adjoining the former Great House
Farm / Church View Close land.

I have made a narrowed FOI request to the Vale of Glamorgan Council (case
00211484) seeking the instruction, works order, authorisation and any
record linking the tree to the Williams/Buckler family or to the 1988
demolition.

More generally, I am concerned that parts of the planning and land-history
record which could bear upon the ownership history are incomplete or
unavailable. I am not presently asking the CPS to draw an inference from
that absence. I ask that any potentially relevant records held by public
authorities or other custodians be identified and preserved while the
police and other investigations are ongoing.

5. Existing correspondence and preservation

I have maintained a continuous documentary record of communications
concerning these issues with:

- South Wales Police, including FOI, SAR, crime-recording and preservation
correspondence;
- HM Land Registry and the Independent Complaints Reviewer (ICR/090/26);
- Cadw, Heneb, RCAHMW, Glamorgan Archives, National Library of Wales and
other heritage bodies; and
- Vale of Glamorgan Council, including FOI requests and internal reviews.

Preservation requests/notices have also been made to principal
record-holders where I consider material may be relevant, so that
potentially significant evidence is not inadvertently destroyed,
transferred or disposed of while these matters are being examined.

6. Request to CPS Cymru-Wales

I respectfully ask CPS Cymru-Wales to:

(a) note the South Wales Police crime-recording request of 28 September
2026 and HM Land Registry reference 260202-5732372 as the present principal
references, with any subsequent police or Report █████ reference to be
added when available;

(b) ensure that the material is considered by the appropriate CPS
prosecutor or team if it is referred for prosecutorial consideration,
including consideration of whether the █████ documentary conduct raises
sufficiently serious or complex criminal issues to require specialist
casework;

(c) note that, should a private prosecution subsequently be instituted, I
may make a specific request for the CPS to consider the Director's power
under section 6(2) of the Prosecution of Offences Act 1985; and

(d) advise me of the appropriate procedure for making such a request, and
the evidence CPS would require, if that stage is reached.

I appreciate that the CPS does not itself conduct the police investigation.
My purpose at this stage is to ensure that the potential prosecutorial
dimension is properly identified and that the present material is capable
of being matched to any police investigation or later referral.

I remain ready to provide an indexed evidential bundle comprising the 1955
and 1974 material, historical conveyances and plans, HM Land Registry
documentation for WA231076, WA240304 and related titles, relevant court
records, chronology, and photographs concerning the former property and
subsequent works. The website provides a public index to much of this
material.

I note the previous deadline of 13 October 2026. I will provide any South
Wales Police crime/incident reference or Report █████ reference as soon as
it is allocated.

Yours sincerely,

Requester
